## Student Workflow

Students do not create Quarto or HTML documents. For each project they:

1. download the assigned synthetic CSV and starter code;
2. complete the marked sections of the MATLAB or R script;
3. run the script to generate figures and results CSV files;
4. complete a supplied Word or Google Docs report template;
5. export the report as PDF;
6. submit the PDF, source code, and generated CSV outputs.

## Download the Report Templates

- [Project 1 Word template](templates/project1-report-template.docx)
- [Project 2 Word template](templates/project2-report-template.docx)
- [Common printable data dictionary](handouts/data-dictionary.pdf)

The `.docx` files work in Microsoft Word and can also be uploaded to Google
Drive and opened in Google Docs. Replace the short prompts, insert figures and
tables, keep the supplied section order, and download or export the finished
document as PDF. No document coding is required.

## Project 1 File Contract

Replace `01` with the assigned group number.

```text
group-01-project-1.pdf
group_01_project1.m
model_rmse.m
group-01-project1-results.csv
```

MATLAB code filenames use underscores because MATLAB identifiers cannot contain
hyphens. The starter script writes the results file using the exact fields in
the [Project 1 result contract](project-result-contracts.qmd).

## Project 2 File Contract

```text
group-01-project-2.pdf
group-01-project2.R
group-01-project2-results.csv
group-01-validation-predictions.csv
```

The starter R script writes both CSV files. Students should not type or edit
the calculated values manually. Exact cleaning, metric, and prediction rules are
given in the [Project 2 result contract](project-result-contracts.qmd).

## PDF Report Outline

The supplied document templates contain headings and short prompts.
Students replace the prompts with their figures, results, and explanations.

```text
Title and group identifier
1. Problem and assigned dataset
2. Data checks
3. Required figures and numerical results
4. Model or fitted relationship
5. Validation or sensitivity check
6. Conclusion and limitations
7. AI-use appendix
```

The PDF should contain the important equations, figures, tables, and
interpretations, but not pages of source code.

## AI-Use Appendix

| Tool | Task or prompt | Output used? | What was changed or rejected? | Student check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
|  |  |  |  |  |

If no generative AI was used, state that explicitly.

## Group Contribution Statement

Every submission includes a contribution statement signed by all group members.

| Student | Principal contribution | Work checked by |
|---|---|---|
|  |  |  |

Signing confirms that each student has reviewed the final submission and accepts
responsibility for understanding its code, figures, results, and conclusions.

## Machine-Readable Results Principle

The generated results files are part of the assessment. They connect the report
to executable code and allow every group's numerical claims to be checked.

The checker will confirm that:

- the assigned group dataset was used;
- required fields are present;
- reported values can be independently reproduced;
- predictions align with the correct observations;
- the PDF does not contradict the computational output.
